name: Reverse Jade Lizard
summary: Sell an OTM call and an OTM put credit spread in the same expiry; the mirror image of the jade lizard, with no downside risk when the credit exceeds the put spread width, and uncapped risk to the upside.

legs.strike_rule: short put strike - Wp, with Wp chosen so total credit > Wp x 100; typically 1.0-2.0% of spot

when_to_use: IV rank > 50 with steep PUT skew (index ETFs), where the put spread pays enough to exceed its own width. Structurally attractive on SPY/QQQ because put skew is persistently rich - but the naked short call makes it Level 4.
max_profit: net credit received, if the underlying finishes between the short put and the short call
max_loss: UNDEFINED to the upside (naked short call). No downside loss when credit > put spread width.
breakevens: upside breakeven = short call strike + credit/100; NO downside breakeven when credit > Wp x 100

greeks.delta: negative at entry (-10 to -25 per unit)

entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: the short call is uncovered, which requires Alpaca options level 4. The order router must reject this slug while the account is Level 3.
Level 4 version: total credit must exceed put spread width x 100.
Level 4 version: short call delta 0.20-0.30, short put delta -0.20 to -0.30, IV rank >= 50.

A Level-3-legal substitute exists: add a long call above the short call (converting it to a call credit spread), which turns the structure into an iron condor variant and gives up the 'no downside risk' property.
management_rules: Level 4 only: close at 50% of the credit.
Level 4 only: close or roll at 21 DTE.
Level 4 only: close if the short call delta reaches 0.45, or if spot trades above the short call strike at any time.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: naked short call - flatten by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short call immediately if it is ITM with extrinsic < $0.10; an uncovered call assignment creates a naked short stock position.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the short call before every ex-dividend date whenever it is ITM - uncovered short calls are the single most commonly assigned option ahead of dividends.
Close the short put if ITM with extrinsic < $0.10, and by 2 DTE unconditionally.
assignment_risk: Worst-in-family for the call leg: uncovered short call assignment delivers -100 shares with no offsetting long, an unlimited liability and an immediate margin call on a $50k account. The put spread's short leg is the ordinary 100-share purchase risk.
buying_power: Naked short call margin (approximately max(20% of underlying value - OTM amount, 10% of strike value) + premium) plus (Wp x 100 - put spread credit).
common_mistakes: Trading it without naked-call approval; assuming symmetry with the jade lizard (it is far more dangerous because upside risk is unbounded while downside risk was merely large); ignoring dividend assignment on the short call.
zero_dte_notes: Never. An uncovered 0DTE short call on an American-style ETF is the highest-severity assignment scenario this bank contains.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
